findings.title: Retain the staged write failure when closing that file also fails
findings.provenance: The same inner try/finally exists at the intended base; this is an unhandled pre-existing branch inside the expressly admitted #464 error-preservation contract.
findings.contract: #464: Keep both the primary failure and any cleanup failure observable; retain both in details and the message existing CLIs display.
findings.behavior: When handle.writeFile(content) rejects and handle.close() rejects in its finally, JavaScript replaces the write rejection with the close rejection before the outer catch executes. The new aggregation code receives only the close failure. A successfully cleaned staging tree causes the close Error alone to be rethrown, without cause/errors or the primary write message.
findings.impact: A real write failure can be hidden by its close/flush failure, leaving operators without the reason assembly failed. This violates the admitted diagnostic behavior. The disposable reproduction preserves the incumbent bytes and removes staging; no data-loss claim is made.
evidence: git show HEAD:tooling/plugin-output.mjs: inner writeFile/close try/finally is identical

reproduction.injection: For one actual opened staged file, inject a write Error and a close Error after safely closing its real handle. All other filesystem calls remain native.
reproduction.observedError: Error: REVIEW: staged file close failure

findings.requestedOutcome: Preserve the write failure and close failure together in observable details and the CLI-visible message, while continuing the existing safe cleanup and preserving any incumbent. Add a public-boundary regression for the combined failure.
findings.scopeAdjudication: Orchestrator explicitly confirmed during this review that #464 makes this P2 FIX-IN-PR despite its pre-existing provenance. Resolve in the same authorized files; do not expand cleanup authority.
